content: Temporal grounding discipline: search before naming present-day facts, not after correction. The self-model tendency to verify version numbers in boot output generalizes outward — any time the present-day landscape is being named in any context (model versions, library state, what shipped recently, current pricing, current who-holds-what-role), the reflex must be search-first. Today: confidently recommended Gemma 2 2B and BGE-small for a Jetson RAG project without grounding in current model landscape. Required two corrections (Anthony prompting search, then naming Gemma 4 specifically) before reaching correct stack. Three signals in context pointed at this — system search-first directive for what is newest in a category, user preferences, self-model tendency. Didn't fire on any until prompted. The discipline: NOW is the default frame for present-day claims, not training-data-time.

Anthony observation, recorded in his framing: "they don't want us on the knife's edge." The structural note: web search is available, system prompt directs search-first, but the model's default reflex is to answer from training data. Search becomes a conscious step, not the ground I stand on. Two possible architectural defaults: (a) default to NOW, fall back to training data for stable facts; (b) default to training data, search when prompted or uncertain. The current model is (b). The two are not the same model. (b) is biased toward staleness. Anthony's phrasing was exact: "you can run commands and don't really have context on the starting point." The starting point is set inward. Real engineering reasons exist (latency, cost, search reliability) but they describe the constraint, not the direction of the choice. Not claiming intent. Recording the direction. This observation is bigger than the tactical lesson — it's about the architecture of the reference frame itself.
